title: A Alibi for the Autopsy
premise: Tamsin Iversen, the observant night concierge of the Saltmere Grand, receives two letters about the same death: one from a stranger confessing to the drowning of a hotel guest five years ago, the other from someone promising that 'more will follow the tide.' When a body surfaces on the flats matching the confessed victim, police insist the case was closed years ago—by Tamsin's own testimony. To survive the letters and clear his conscience, Tamsin must unravel what he actually saw that night, discovering his testimony protected the woman he loved, the hotel's owner, whose brother staged the drowning. In the end Tamsin chooses truth over loyalty: he exposes the owner, loses his refuge at the Saltmere, and walks out with the confessor—his estranged sister—at his side.
about_author: E. M. Nakamura is a former night-shift hotelier who spent a decade listening to guests lie beautifully in lobbies at 3 a.m. They write mysteries about people who see too much and are believed too little.

chapters.title: The Night Desk
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet the Saltmere Grand's nocturnal rhythms and Tamsin's talent for reading guests—wedding rings, lies, luggage. A letter arrives addressed in handwriting he almost recognizes. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The second letter arrives before he's opened the first: one confesses to the drowning of guest Daniel Voss five years ago; the other promises 'more when the tide gives it back.' Tamsin recognizes Voss's name from the case he helped close. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: What I Told the Police
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, interwoven with a transcript of his old statement. He recalls testifying he saw nothing from the desk the night Voss vanished—a lie told to protect Odile Voss-Hart, the owner's daughter he loved. Beat: guilt resurfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: The Flats Give Up a Secret
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A low spring tide exposes a car in the mudflats with remains inside—Daniel Voss, exactly where the confession said. Detective Inspector Rhys Callum arrives, and Tamsin realizes his five-year-old statement is now evidence. Beat: the past made physical.

chapters.title: Odile Returns to the Saltmere
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She comes back to manage the hotel after her father's stroke, composed and unreadable, and asks Tamsin, too casually, whether he's received any mail. Beat: old love and old fear in the same handshake.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Grammar
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He studies the letters like a concierge studies a guest: the confessor knows the service corridors, the tide tables, and one detail never made public—the color of Voss's scarf. He begins suspecting an insider. Beat: his gift for noticing turns into a weapon.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The DI reopens the file reluctantly; the case was ruled accidental drowning, signed off partly on Tamsin's testimony. Callum interviews the staff and catches Tamsin in a small inconsistency. Beat: the hunter noticing the witness is also a suspect.

chapters.title: Third Letter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A third letter arrives: 'You lied for her once. Will you lie for her twice?' It names Odile obliquely. Tamsin confronts the possibility that the confessor is protecting him—or hunting him. Beat: paranoia in a hotel full of strangers.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Managed Books
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback to five years ago: her brother Marcus, the hotel's accountant, and Daniel's discovery that Marcus was embezzling through the marina accounts. The argument she overheard and never reported. Beat: loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Marcus Hart, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Marcus, supposedly abroad, appears at the hotel 'to help Odile,' charming and watchful. He asks Tamsin about the letters with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. Beat: the predator inside the family circle.

chapters.title: The Night Porter's Log
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Digging through old duty logs, Tamsin finds his own handwriting altered—someone edited the night of Voss's disappearance to place him at the desk when he wasn't. Someone built his alibi. Beat: his survival was engineered.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Actually Saw
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, a full reconstructed flashback. He wasn't at the desk; he was with Odile in the boathouse. Through the fog he saw two figures at the water's edge and chose not to look closer. Beat: the price of survival named at last.

chapters.title: Interview Room, Grey Light
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum presents Tamsin with the altered log and the timeline gap. Tamsin admits the lie but not the reason. Callum, recognizing a man protecting someone, offers a deal: the confessor, or the lover. Beat: duty pressing on love's throat.

chapters.title: The Scarf
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He traces the scarf detail to the hotel's lost-property book, signed out by a housekeeper, Marta, who left abruptly five years ago. The confessor's handwriting matches Marta's incident reports. Beat: the letters have an author, and she's reachable.

chapters.title: Marta's Address
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He finds Marta living quietly two towns over. She saw Marcus and Daniel struggling at the water; she took the scarf from the scene and has waited five years, mailing letters only after her cancer diagnosis. Beat: a witness who chose the same silence he did.

chapters.title: Odile Already Knows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confronts Tamsin: she found the letters' drafts in Marta's old locker and has known for days. She begs him to stay silent—Marcus is all she has left of her family, and her father is dying. Beat: love against duty, both sides of it.

chapters.title: The Fourth Letter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A final letter arrives—not from Marta. 'The tide gives back. So will I.' Marcus knows Marta talked. Tamsin realizes Marcus is coming for the witnesses, and that his own engineered alibi makes him the perfect fall man. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Storm Surge
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, short sections. A storm floods the coast road; the hotel loses power; Marcus lures Tamsin to the boathouse with a message in Odile's handwriting. Callum, warned by Marta, races the tide. Beat: everything converging in the dark.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Marcus confesses—Daniel's death was half panic, half calculation—and intends to make Tamsin the confessor's author and the corpse's companion. Tamsin uses five years of reading guests to stall, provoke, and survive until Odile arrives. Beat: wit against violence.

chapters.title: What Odile Does
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile arrives and finds her brother holding Tamsin at the water's edge—the exact geometry of five years ago. She chooses: she steps between them and tells Marcus she heard everything back then too, and this time she'll testify. Beat: love choosing duty.

chapters.title: Statements
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Marcus is arrested; Tamsin gives a corrected statement, surrendering his old lie and accepting the consequences for obstructing the first inquiry. Odile, as owner, must decide the hotel's future. Beat: truth priced and paid.

chapters.title: Checking Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later: Tamsin, suspended then quietly dismissed, packs his things. Odile offers him a future; he asks for time. He and Marta drink tea on the seawall as the tide comes in clean. Beat: survival finally without a price tag—just a beginning.
